intro: Outlook for medical billers on Mac is the same Outlook for Mac app as everywhere else, with a few settings that matter more for claims. Save repeat denial replies with File > Save As Template, and sort payer mail with server rules. Lazur can point at each menu and walk you through it, but it does not click for you.
tldr: Outlook for medical billers on Mac runs the same app as everyone else. The newest feature entry is version 16.114, from October 14, 2026.
Built-in templates need Microsoft 365 and Outlook for Mac 15.35 (170610) or later. Save a reply with File > Save As Template.
Server rules run from top to bottom. Stop processing more rules is on by default, so put narrow rules first.
Legacy Outlook for Mac stops working with Exchange Online mailboxes from October 2026. Turn off the Legacy Outlook switch now.
Lazur points, guides, dictates and drafts. It does not click buttons for you.

blocks.text: Most mail in a billing inbox follows a few patterns. Payers send remittance notices, requests for records, and denial letters. Patients ask about balances. Your team sends status checks, corrected claims, and appeals. The same reply often goes out again and again, which makes templates and rules the first two settings to learn.
How much email a billing day holds

Public numbers on billing inbox volume are thin. No public study measures how much time billers spend in Outlook. The closest data comes from NHS staff. In a survey of 3,047 staff, people estimated about 14 emails a day on average days before the pandemic. On a busy day, they estimated 29. Treat those as a rough guide, not a billing benchmark.

Denials add to the load. In Experian Health's 2024 State of Claims survey of 210 healthcare staff, nearly three in four said claim denials had increased. Respondents named prior authorizations and missing or inaccurate data as leading causes. Each denial usually means a reply, a corrected claim, or an appeal. Each of those means more email.
Check your Outlook version before you change settings

Start with the version. Microsoft's release notes list Outlook for Mac builds by date. The newest feature entry is version 16.114, dated October 14, 2026. A later 16.114.3 build, dated October 27, lists no Outlook feature changes. If your build is older, update before you set up anything new.

Then check the legacy switch. Microsoft says legacy Outlook for Mac stops working against Exchange Online mailboxes starting October 2026. The Exchange Web Services service it relies on retires on October 1, 2026. That date has already passed. If your billing mail still runs in legacy Outlook, check that it loads before you rely on it.

blocks.title: Turn off legacy first
blocks.text: Open legacy Outlook for Mac and turn off the Legacy Outlook switch. You can also run Help > Check for Updates, or update through the App Store. Do this before you build templates or rules, so you do not rebuild them later.
Save denial replies as templates on Mac

Templates save the most time for billers. A denial reply to one payer often changes only a few details. Those details are the claim number, the service dates, and the amount. Write the reply once, mark the details that change, then save it.

items: Open the reply you send most often, or write it in a new message.
Replace the claim number, patient name, and dates with clear blanks, such as [CLAIM NUMBER].
Choose File > Save As Template and give it a name that says the payer and the reason.
Later, choose File > New > Mail From Template and pick the .emltpl file you saved.
Fill in the blanks, read the whole message, and then send.

blocks.text: Built-in template controls need a Microsoft 365 subscription. Your copy of Outlook for Mac must be version 15.35 (170610) or later. If File > New > Mail From Template does not appear, check your version and your subscription first.
Where the My Templates add-in falls short

Microsoft also offers the My Templates add-in. It works only with Microsoft Exchange accounts. It is not available in shared mailboxes opened in Outlook for Mac. Microsoft's general template page says the add-in only stores short text snippets and supports plain text with basic styling. That page does not list Outlook for Mac in its Applies To list, so do not count on it for Mac.

blocks.text: If your claims inbox is a shared mailbox, test the built-in option in your own mailbox first. Then ask your Microsoft 365 admin how the team should share the template file. Do not keep a saved template with patient details in a shared folder.
Sort payer mail with server rules
Rules move payer mail out of your main view. On Mac, Outlook supports only server rules, because Microsoft says client rules are no longer supported. Open them from Outlook > Settings > Rules.

Rules run from top to bottom. Stop processing more rules is on by default, so the first match wins. Put the most specific rule at the top. A broad rule above a narrow one can catch every message before the narrow rule gets its turn.

items: Create a new rule and name it after the payer or the task, such as Payer denials.
Set the condition, such as the sender's domain or a word like denial in the subject.
Set the action, such as moving the message to a folder named Denials.
Check the order. A broader rule above this one wins first.

blocks.title: Test before you trust it
blocks.text: Send yourself a test message that matches the rule. Check that it lands in the right folder. Then send a second test with a non-matching subject. That mail should stay in the inbox.
Recent Outlook for Mac changes that help claim work

Microsoft's release notes list several recent changes. Version 16.111, dated July 14, 2026, lets you edit a message in the Outbox before it sends. If you spot a wrong claim number after you queue a reply, fix it there instead of sending a correction.

Version 16.113, dated September 16, 2026, adds several small fixes. Replies, forwards, and signatures now follow the direction of the message you answer. A Remove button for recipients appears while you compose. Paste Options can convert Markdown to rich text, which helps when you paste notes from another tool.

Two window changes help when you work across many claims. Version 16.112, dated August 11, 2026, adds a Calendar setting that opens new events in a separate window. Version 16.113 also lets you right-click Mail, Calendar, or People in the left rail to open it in its own window. Keep the claims inbox in one window and the calendar in another.
Build a follow-up schedule for claim status

Office Ally's guidance for billers gives three timing rules. Review a claim status 24 to 48 hours after submission. Act on clearinghouse rejections the same business day. Balance and post ERAs within one business day. Those windows are easy to miss without a reminder.

items: On submission day: create a calendar event for the status check.
24 to 48 hours later: check the claim status and note the result.
Same business day as a rejection: fix and resubmit the claim.
Within one business day of an ERA: post the payment and balance the account.

blocks.text: A calendar event is the simplest reminder. Put the claim number in the event title, so you can find it fast. If you prefer Apple Reminders, the same title works there.
A worked example for one denied claim

Suppose a payer denies a claim on Monday because it wants records. You open the saved denial template, add the claim number, and send it that day. You create a calendar event for the next status check, inside the 24 to 48 hour window. If the payer answers with a second denial, you start from a second template. The Denials folder rule catches the reply, so nothing sits in the main inbox.
Mistakes billers make in Outlook on Mac

items: Saving a template with a real patient name or member ID in it.
Counting on My Templates in a shared mailbox, then wondering why it is missing.
Writing rules without checking their order, so a broad rule catches everything.
Staying on legacy Outlook after the October 2026 cutoff.
Setting a status check with no reminder, so it slips past the 24 to 48 hour window.
Asking an assistant about a screen with patient data before checking your practice policy.

blocks.text: How Lazur helps with Outlook on Mac

That still matters in a billing office. A screen can show a patient name, a date of birth, or a member ID. This page makes no HIPAA claim about Lazur. faq.question: Is there a separate version of Outlook for medical billers on Mac?
faq.answer: No. Medical billers use the same Outlook for Mac app as everyone else. The newest feature entry in Microsoft's notes is version 16.114, dated October 14, 2026. Use Help > Check for Updates to get the newest build.

faq.question: Do built-in email templates need Microsoft 365?
faq.answer: Yes. Microsoft says built-in template controls require a Microsoft 365 subscription and Outlook for Mac version 15.35 (170610) or later. Check that File > New > Mail From Template appears before you rely on it.

faq.question: Why don't My Templates show up in our shared billing mailbox?
faq.answer: Microsoft says the My Templates add-in is not available in shared mailboxes opened in Outlook for Mac. It also works only with Exchange accounts. Test the built-in template option in your own mailbox, then ask your admin how to share the file.

faq.question: Why do my rules file mail in the wrong folder?
faq.answer: Rules run from top to bottom, and Stop processing more rules is on by default. The first match wins. Move the narrow rule above the broad one, then test again with a sample message.

faq.question: Does legacy Outlook for Mac still work with claims mail?
faq.answer: Microsoft says legacy Outlook for Mac stops working against Exchange Online mailboxes starting October 2026. The service it relies on retires on October 1, 2026. Turn off the Legacy Outlook switch or update the app, then confirm your mail loads.

faq.question: Can Lazur click through Outlook for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons or operate other apps for you. It points, guides you one click at a time, answers out loud, and drafts or dictates text. You stay in control of every click and every send.
